newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Transpower expects to equal last yr's profit.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Transpower expects to equal last yr's profit.

text.p: New Zealand's state-owned electricity grid operator Transpower said on Tuesday it was confident of equalling in 1996/97 last year's annual net surplus attributable to shareholders of NZ$95.9 million.

Chief executive Bob Thomson told Reuters that Transpower expected its profit to be level with last year's, despite some revenue problems in the first month of operation of New Zealand's new wholesale electricity market.
"We plan to be level and I think in the end we will be level...with last year," he said.

"We were targeting NZ$95 million again this year, but we are always conservative. I could see it going a bit above that. Don't get me wrong, I've got short term problems with getting the revenue streams lined up (in the new wholesale electricity marketplace), but I've got a lot of people helping me," Thomson said. -- Wellington Newsroom 64 4 4734746
